substrate.title: Substrate
substrate.active: Intelligence does not exist in isolation. It emerges within physical and computational constraints — space, time, energy, and hardware. These limits define what is possible long before reasoning or learning begins.

reactivity.title: Reactivity
reactivity.active: Before planning or understanding, systems must respond. Reactivity is fast, automatic, and unavoidable — a layer of immediate response that operates without deliberation or intent.

world_models.title: World Models
world_models.active: Intelligence learns by simulating reality internally. World models allow a system to imagine outcomes, test actions, and explore possibilities before committing to them.

organization.title: Organization
organization.active: Intelligence is not singular. It emerges from many specialized processes working together — coordinated into a structured system capable of coherent behavior.

emergence.title: Emergence
emergence.active: Complex behavior does not require central control. From simple interactions and local rules, unexpected patterns and structures arise naturally over time.

symbiosis.title: Symbiosis
symbiosis.active: The goal is not replacement, but alignment. Human values and artificial intelligence must evolve together, shaping and constraining one another to ensure meaningful progress.
